tagline: Leading Michigan energy utility committed to reliable, affordable clean energy transition
hero_kpi_rationale: The Capex KPI is selected as the hero metric because it captures the primary driver of DTE's future growth: massive investments in electric grid modernization, energy transition, and new clean generation and storage capacity, aligned with binding regulatory requirements and Michigan state standards.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures (2026-2030)
kpis.explanation: Total amount invested annually in electric, gas, and energy transition infrastructure projects from 2026 to 2030.
kpis.description: DTE plans $30 billion for DTE Electric, $4.5 billion for DTE Gas, and $2 billion for DTE Vantage from 2026 to 2030, totaling $36.5 billion.
kpis.signal: Large-scale, structural five-year investment to modernize the grid and decarbonize

kpis.name: Operating Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenues generated by the company's operations during the fiscal year.
kpis.description: $15.8 billion in operating revenue in 2025, according to the MD&A.
kpis.signal: Stable revenues around $15-16 billion, typical of a regulated utility

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Net profit attributable to the company after all expenses.
kpis.description: Net income attributable to DTE Energy was $1.462 billion in 2025, up 4.1% from $1.404 billion in 2024.

kpis.name: Earnings Per Share
kpis.explanation: Diluted earnings attributable to common shareholders divided by the number of shares outstanding.
kpis.description: Diluted earnings per share were $7.03 in 2025, compared to $6.77 in 2024, an increase of 3.8%.
kpis.signal: Sustained EPS growth, indicating financial discipline

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Annual consolidated revenue, values extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL for the last five fiscal years reported in 10-K filings.
kpis.signal: $12.607 billion in revenue in the latest year.

kpis.name: Clean Generation Investments
kpis.explanation: Investments dedicated to renewable energy, battery storage, and decarbonization from 2026 to 2030.
kpis.description: DTE Electric plans $15 billion in investments in clean generation (renewables, battery storage, etc.) from 2026 to 2030.
kpis.signal: $15 billion allocated to clean generation from 2026 to 2030

kpis.name: Coal Units Retired or Planned for Retirement
kpis.explanation: Total number of coal-fired generation units retired or scheduled for retirement.
kpis.description: DTE has retired 11 coal units (Trenton Channel, River Rouge, St. Clair, Belle River) and plans to retire the remaining 5 (Monroe and Belle River) by 2032, aligned with its net-zero carbon goal by 2050.
kpis.signal: Energy transition underway with retirement of 16 coal units by 2032

risks.title: Regulatory and Rate Risks
risks.score_rationale: This risk is mentioned early (page 18) and is central to the company's business model. The intensity of language ('negatively impacted', 'disallow recovery', 'unfavorable rate relief') underscores its severity. It directly affects the ability to recover costs and finance planned massive investments ($36.5 billion).

risks.title: Environmental Regulatory Risks
risks.score_rationale: This risk is detailed across several paragraphs (pages 18-19) and covers critical areas such as emissions, waste, and climate change. The language ('significantly increase capital spending', 'negatively affect the affordability') indicates high severity. It impacts spending and long-term planning.

risks.title: Risks Related to Renewable Energy Investments
risks.score_rationale: This risk is addressed on page 19 and concerns clean and renewable energy standards, as well as energy waste reduction programs. The language ('significantly increase capital expenditures') shows a potentially significant impact. It is tied to the energy transition mandated by Michigan legislation (100% clean energy by 2040).

risks.title: Risks Related to Distribution System Operations
risks.score_rationale: This risk is described on page 20 and concerns aging electric and gas infrastructure. The phrase 'material adverse effect' and references to operational failures ('operational failure') highlight its severity. It directly affects service continuity and maintenance costs.

risks.title: Risks Related to Extreme Weather Conditions
risks.score_rationale: This risk is detailed on page 20 with emphasis on increasing frequency of extreme weather events. The language ('material unplanned expenses', 'expenses may not be fully recoverable') indicates high severity. It impacts expenses and cost recovery, with potential reputational damage.

ai_positioning.summary: The company DTE has no significant mentions of artificial intelligence, machine learning, or similar technologies in the provided excerpts from its 10-K/20-F report.
